account: Today I kept morning office hours and the ten o'clock grain inspection, and have now returned home for a late noon lunch before council letters at thirteen. The builder reported west-bank roads passable, no confirmed hazards, and a zero repair estimate. No repairs or spending have been authorized; future work needs an approved itemized price. The unusual business is a repeated, vague rumour about a bridge or port change at the bakery. Several townsfolk repeat much the same phrase, and the neighbour has heard it too, but nobody has given me a specific change or firsthand confirmation. I asked the builder to clarify the remark with the baker. I cannot yet say whether it concerns a real proposal, a misunderstanding, or something else. At the mill I saw 128 hay bales in the sale chest and left them untouched. That establishes stock on hand, not quality or delivery needs. Neither the neighbour nor freight could identify the manager or confirm shortages or delivery orders. Freight says the warehouse was empty when last checked and has storage available; he will ask the baker about grain transport and report a definite request before moving stock. His stated purpose is to offer ferry and delivery services, not to carry out any confirmed bridge or port change. The neighbour expects me for our usual three o'clock tea at the dockside cottage. For now the town's practical business seems to be routine supplies, transport availability, and checking an unverified rumour rather than responding to an established emergency.
